programmes.d: Mike and Vicki say their 37-year-old son was once making millions of dollars running a successful real estate company, but now lives with them, on their dime; he blames them for his current living situation.
The doctor gives self-help advice and strategies for a healthy life.
A look at what happens when an unhealthy relationship threatens to tear a mother and daughter apart; Geisel says her 18-year-old daughter is boyfriend-obsessed and is damaging her promising future.
The doctor helps mothers with secrets and lies: A woman fears her addiction to painkillers will tear her family apart; a grandmother steals; a woman confesses a 29-year-old secret to her daughter.
Two families desperate to find their missing children ask Dr. Phil for help. Two-year-old Bianca disappeared while in the care of her father. He says she was taken when he was carjacked.
A guest says she will dump her boyfriend if he does not propose soon; a woman says her marriage is a sham.
Despite maintaining his innocence, Jack McCullough, once known as John Tessier, is convicted of the 1957 murder of 7-year-old Maria Ridulph.
Guests with drug addictions.
A woman says her 19-year-old daughter has fallen for a "bad boy," and she worries about her safety.
High-school students with two children.
Mixed signals; body language; actions versus words; self-confidence.
Rachel confronts her sister's ex-boyfriend, whom she accuses of killing the 14-year-old girl in 1985.

A woman says her fiancé pouts, whines and stomps his feet whenever they get into an argument; a woman says it is time for her common-law husband to stop partying with his friends and take care of his family.
Actors Dennis Quaid and Rene Russo ("Yours, Mine and Ours"); a blended family struggles to get along.
A man thinks his son-in-law had something to do with his daughter's disappearance.

A prominent family has been tied to the deaths of a housekeeper, a high school classmate, and a young woman in a boat crash; in 2021, Alex Murdaugh reportedly found his wife and son shot dead on their property, setting off a bizarre chain of events.
A young woman tells who she blames for her addiction problems.
The family of a former finalist on "America's Next Top Model" says she is losing her battle with drug addiction, and Dr. Phil steps in to help.

Parents do not believe that their 19-year-old son committed suicide, and two witnesses agree to take polygraph tests to clear the cloud of suspicion they say follows them as the result of the parents' allegations.
Feuding neighbors.
High-school students with two children.
Guests with immature spouses.
A woman says her husband wants her to consider an open marriage.

Treva's daughters say she is a violent alcoholic who might be better off behind bars; Treva, who has been to rehab eight times, says that they do not work for her, and that her whole family needs an intervention.
Advice for dealing with moochers.

Kristen says she isn't a hoarder but admits that her "collection of things" is creating a problem: she is running out of room; why she says it is hard for her to part with her belongings; friends say that her "hoarding" is keeping her isolated.
Guests say their loved ones are too controlling, combative and outspoken.
Former spokesman Willie Jessop of the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints talks of crimes that took place within the polygamous sect.
Guests seek help fulfilling New Year's resolutions; TV-show host Jim Cramer ("Mad Money") offers a strategy for achieving financial resolutions in 2009.

A woman finds her son unconscious in his room with drug paraphernalia surrounding his body; the doctor makes a surprise house call to insist a drug-abusing teen get help immediately; an alcoholic stay-at-home mother.
A self-proclaimed runaway bride; a man says weddings are too expensive; a woman who says her fiancé dumped her six days before the wedding.
Courtney says her divorced mother traded in her children for a life of parties, drinking and men, resulting in two DUIs and a car accident that nearly killed her.
